questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly going to a city and a part of Europe I had not been to before, and get the chance to really experience the place over a longer period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it a bt hard to find information, especially in terms of courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When arriving to the university we got some general information about social things and school related info

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to find a place through a friend of a friend

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is a good experience to find something on your own and live with people from the host country, if possible

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found it confusing and a lot of the courses from the additional list was not offered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was help at the international office, but they seemed to be to few people working there, so it was hard getting help when you needed it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed in the end because I was allowed by masters teachers to join some of their courses, but I did not get all the courses I initially wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice them to take a good look at the courses available, and maybe have a plan b if the courses boy planned to take are not offered, or does not match each other in the schedule

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses I did not really think matched the level at UCPH, but also the courses are smaller so it is hard to compare fully.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was usually more loose, but it was also more normal with smaller classes, which I really liked.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Wellbeing and Health Promotion at the Workplace
Altered States of Consciousness and Hypnosis
Culture and Psychology
Culture and Society
Introduction to Counseling Psychology
Leadership and Organizational Studies
Psychological Ethics and Legal Issues
Study and Communication Skills

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Altered States of Consciousness and Hypnosis class, and also heard a lot of good things about the Psychedelics class and Sex Education class. I think they are all a bit unique for the university and the teachers of the courses are some of the best in their fields.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Did not really encounter any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries was more expensive than expected. Public transport and city bikes are really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of activities at all times, and you also have the opportunity to have sports as elective courses. There was a lot of different sports, a lot of city life events, and also more casual clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing some kind of sports. It is also cheaper than in Denmark to do sports in Hungary. I would also recommend going hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot of good hiking trips outside and inside the city, a lot of culture and architecture to see, and also fun nightlife.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was not too hard, also because you share the experience with other exchange students. But of course there is small cultural differences that will be weird in the beginning, but also super interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think going to local events, they use Facebook a lot for events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I was surprised by the temperament of the people in Hungary, because I was not used to people yelling in public, but people are also very sweet. It can also be a bit hard to get used to seeing poverty and homeless people a lot more than in Copenhagen

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really loved the cultural life with a lot of live music, folk music, folk dance, and cool authentic places where you could hang out both day and evening

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be a bit proactive with finding courses in the beginning and then it will probably work out
Don't stress too much with the social events in the introduction week, there is plenty of chances to meet people 
Don't stress about the exams, even though there might be many

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the social part, and also experiencing the city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing spending time with new friends, doing all the things you wanted to experience, having people to visit and also getting alone time could be challenging

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
